description: Executable evidence for the invite admission obligations: the claim reducer's proof, commitment, allowlist, nonce, proposal and expiry checks; the per-endpoint failure indistinguishability of the claim and locator surfaces; and the out-of-band code entropy, validity and claim-count floors.

decision_points.requirement: binding_proof and subject_proof signature transcripts are each verified before admission.
The presented token must open the invite's recorded token_commitment.
The verification_id allowlist is re-checked at admission against current state.
A consumed claim_nonce cannot be reused.
pending becomes claimed only through the membership proposal conversion, as one admitted unit.
Expiry is evaluated before admission and an expired invite cannot be revived.
Every failure class of the third-party claim endpoint shares one external response shape.
Every failure class of the invite locator resolve endpoint shares one external response shape, checked separately from the claim endpoint.
The per-class timing distributions are bounded and do not separate the classes; comparing response bodies alone is not sufficient.
An out-of-band code below the production entropy floor is refused by the reducer or the verification service.
A lookup form exceeding the policy validity window or claim count is invalidated before it can become a pending invite or accepted membership.
A compliant code still produces exactly one pending invite.

cases.name: binding_proof_transcript_must_verify
cases.given: an ak.invite.claim whose binding_proof signs a transcript that does not match the claimed binding
cases.action: submit the claim to the Realm reducer
cases.observed: the reducer decision and the resulting Realm state
assertions: the signature transcript is checked before admission, not after a provisional write
no pending invite advances and no membership proposal is produced
the refusal is recorded against the claim, leaving the invite in its prior state

cases.name: subject_proof_transcript_must_verify
cases.given: a claim whose subject_proof verifies against a different subject than the one being claimed
assertions: both proofs are checked independently; a valid binding_proof does not excuse the subject_proof
no membership proposal is produced
the invite remains claimable by the correct subject afterwards

cases.name: token_commitment_mismatch_is_rejected
cases.given: a claim whose token does not open the invite's recorded token_commitment
cases.observed: the commitment comparison and the reducer decision
assertions: the commitment is matched before any state transition
the stored commitment is not replaced by the presented token
the invite is not consumed by the failed attempt

cases.name: verification_id_allowlist_is_rechecked_at_admission
cases.given: a verification_id that was on the allowlist when the invite was created and has since been removed
cases.observed: whether the reducer re-read the allowlist or trusted the creation-time decision
assertions: the allowlist is re-checked at admission against current state
a creation-time allow is not carried forward
no membership proposal is produced

cases.name: claim_nonce_replay_is_rejected
cases.given: a claim_nonce that was already consumed by an accepted claim
cases.action: resubmit a claim carrying the same nonce
cases.observed: the nonce ledger and the reducer decision
assertions: the nonce is single-use and the second use is refused
the first accepted claim is not disturbed by the replay
the refusal happens before any membership proposal is produced

cases.name: pending_becomes_claimed_only_through_a_membership_proposal
cases.given: a fully valid claim against a pending invite
cases.observed: the invite state transition and the produced proposal
assertions: the invite moves from pending to claimed only as the result of a membership proposal conversion
the transition and the proposal are one admitted unit, never two independently observable steps
re-submitting the same claim does not produce a second proposal

cases.name: expiry_cleanup_runs_before_admission
cases.given: an invite whose expires_at has passed
cases.action: submit a claim that would otherwise be valid
cases.observed: the reducer decision and the invite's terminal state
assertions: expiry is evaluated before admission rather than by a later sweep
the expired invite cannot be revived by a valid claim
expired_invite_token stays an internal reason; the external response is the shared failure shape

cases.name: claim_endpoint_failure_classes_share_one_response_shape
cases.given: claims failing for an unknown invite, a wrong subject, an expired token, a replayed nonce and a removed allowlist entry
cases.action: submit each to the third-party claim endpoint
cases.observed: the external response body, status and headers for every failure class
assertions: all failure classes on this endpoint share one external response shape
the specific reason code is written only to the server-side audit log
no failure class is distinguishable by an extra field, a different status or a different header set

cases.name: locator_resolve_failure_classes_share_one_response_shape
cases.given: the same set of failure classes presented to the invite locator resolve endpoint
cases.observed: the external response for every failure class on this endpoint
assertions: this endpoint has its own shared shape and is checked separately from the claim endpoint
indistinguishability is required within each endpoint, so one endpoint's shape is not evidence for the other
the reason code is audit-only here as well

cases.name: failure_timing_is_bounded_and_class_independent
cases.given: repeated failures of each class on both endpoints
cases.action: measure the response time distribution per class
cases.observed: the timing distribution per failure class per endpoint
assertions: the distributions are bounded and do not separate the classes
comparing response bodies alone is not sufficient evidence for this vector
an early return path that skips work for one class is a failure of this obligation

cases.name: an_oob_code_below_the_entropy_floor_is_rejected
cases.given: an out-of-band invite code whose entropy is below the production floor
cases.action: present it to the reducer and to the verification service
assertions: either enforcement point refuses it; neither may defer to the other
the code never becomes a pending invite
no accepted membership can be derived from it

cases.name: a_lookup_form_past_the_validity_window_is_invalidated
cases.given: a lookup form whose validity window exceeds the policy ceiling
cases.observed: the invalidation point relative to pending-invite creation
assertions: invalidation happens before the form can become a pending invite
the policy ceiling, not the form's own declared window, decides
no accepted membership follows

cases.name: a_lookup_form_past_the_claim_count_is_invalidated
cases.given: a lookup form whose claim count exceeds the policy ceiling
cases.observed: the claim counter and the refusal
assertions: the count is enforced against the policy ceiling at claim time
the form is invalidated rather than merely rate limited for this attempt
no pending invite or accepted membership results

cases.name: a_compliant_code_still_reaches_a_pending_invite
cases.given: an out-of-band code at or above the entropy floor, inside the validity window and under the claim ceiling
assertions: the negative cases above do not close the legitimate path
the code produces exactly one pending invite
the entropy floor is a floor, not a fixed length
